correctness.rationale: The precise \(C^2\) radial, global Hessian and \(\beta>0\) assumptions are stated. Monomials form a complete eigenbasis and covariance strictly orders the eigenvalues. For the radial moment density, the saddle equation \(r\Phi'(r)=n+1/2\) and the Hessian lower bound yield global Gaussian concentration, while the Hessian upper bound gives an \(n\)-uniform denominator lower estimate near the saddle. The expectation-to-symbol ratio differs by \(O(n^{-1/2})\) after scaling. The saddle-mesh derivative estimate captures the entire interval of radial slope limits; monotone spectral inversion and convex secant inequalities prove each iff direction, including all boundary cases. The explicit examples have direct Hessian bounds; a standalone quadrature script checks finite instances but is not used as an infinite-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons identify a motivated gap left by Xu–Dong §5: weaker radial geometric hypotheses for the existence of a Weyl coefficient. An exact all-weight iff, pointwise saddle tracking with uniform remainder, and complete oscillatory cluster interval are stronger than its quadratic theorem and single counterexample. Bdarneh’s inspected Theorem 6.2 supplies only the shared diagonal moment representation. Targeted published-finding corpus queries and own ledgers found no statement whose hypotheses and conclusions imply this theorem. This is a self-review with acknowledged residual risk, not proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: Xu–Dong explicitly ask for weaker asymptotic geometric conditions determining Weyl constants after a Hessian-bounded failure example. The exact iff in the whole natural radially Hessian-bounded class answers this with a concrete disk-averaged curvature invariant; the uniform termwise asymptotic and exact interval of failed-Weyl cluster limits go materially beyond isolated classifications or a routine normalization. A weight with persistently oscillating Hessian but convergent averaged slope and a contrasting nonconvergent example show sharp scope.
